amendments: a correction after the first result keeps this plan, records an amendment with what had been observed, and keeps comparisons interpretable

batch_decision.CROSS_ENGINE_ACQUISITION_MIXED: exactly one QUALIFIED_USEFUL game, or >= 2 useful but an unresolved major inconsistency, or exactly one qualified game; the limiting factor is named
batch_decision.CROSS_ENGINE_ACQUISITION_SUPPORTED: >= 2 games QUALIFIED_USEFUL (each with structural novelty) and no unresolved major evidence inconsistency (no LABEL_POLICY_CONFLICT game, no open review blocker)
batch_decision.EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT: no game is qualified (inputs missing, replay invalid, untraceable, over budget)
batch_decision.open_review_blockers: the number of unresolved BLOCKER findings in the final independent review record; it is printed with the decision
batch_decision.separate: the model-A verdict never changes the batch decision

consistency.audit: ordinary-decode audit of every labelled start has zero length mismatches, non-ordinary decodes and odd starts
consistency.decoders: E starts require agreement of two independent decoders (m68k-disasm walk and the CPU token report), already enforced by `label()`; the accepted-E fraction and rejection classes are reported
consistency.strong_data_conflict: bytes of E code that lie inside an observed DMA-source extent / total E bytes <= 0.005
consistency.weak_conflicts: E bytes that were also ordinary data reads are counted and disclosed; they never gate

control.delivery: amendment of the SEG-080 delivery (frozen before any run): the control is a synthetic `.bk2` that reuses the TAS movie's header, core, controller and sync settings and replaces only the input log, so ROM, core configuration, frame count, tracing and labelling are identical by construction (SEG-080 ran the control with BizHawk default sync settings). The port is tested against the Lua policy.
control.label_inputs: tas = tas_a only; ctl = ctl_a (seed 1); ctl2 = ctl2_a (seed 2); tas_b serves determinism
control.policy: the SEG-080 seeded-input policy (SEG-077 `random`), ported verbatim: input row f (0-based) = policy(f), row 0 empty; seed 1 primary, seed 2 sensitivity; start window 40 s

disclosures: the control moves player 1 only; the two-player TAS movies (Vectorman 2, Earthworm Jim 2) may use player 2
control policy equivalence is to Lua 5.4 integer semantics (tested); SEG-080 fed the same Lua text to BizHawk's interpreter
a title-screen-only control can fail the vblank/reset-PC fidelity check and then yields TRACING_UNAVAILABLE for the game
the native CDL data flag is blanket (for example a boot checksum sweep reads nearly every ROM byte): E bytes that were also read as data are counted and disclosed, never gating
model-A error rates are macro-means over folds (`macro_error_rates`)

emulator.note: BizHawk 2.9.1 linux-x64 under Mono 6.8, Genplus-gx waterbox core, Xvfb, unprivileged user (SEG-080 setup). The Earthworm Jim 2 movie header names 2.6.3: replay on 2.9.1 is attempted first; one bounded compatibility investigation is allowed; 2.6.3 is used only if existing tooling supports it without new instrumentation. No movie input or emulator setting is altered.

identity.procedure: ROM size + SHA-256 equal the frozen table; the movie-header hash field (an MD5 in BizHawk) equals the local ROM MD5; movie SHA-256, input-log SHA-256, frame count, core, emuVersion and the absence of a savestate equal the frozen table; the ROM header serial/region is recorded privately; any ambiguity (several candidate files, a revision mismatch) rejects the game. ROM SHA-1 values quoted in the request are not used as identity.
identity.rom_source: operator-supplied ROMs under games/exp-3-games only; nothing is downloaded or substituted

isolation.checked: SEG-072 corpus manifest (development + sealed), SEG-075/077 candidate lists and their lineage ids; none of the three titles is a sealed or reserved-blind member (machine-checked by image SHA-256/SHA-1 against the manifest's sealed entries; the SEG-077 candidate list is title-level and was checked by hand: Vectorman 2 and Earthworm Jim 2 are sequels of listed development candidates Vectorman and Earthworm Jim and share an engine family with them; they are NOT identical images and are disclosed as engine-adjacent). Image SHA-256 and lineage ids are re-checked against the registry by `analyze` and `diagnose`.
isolation.rule: a title whose image SHA-256 or lineage id appears in the sealed/blind set is excluded and reported

labels.cell_rule: unchanged SEG-072: positive when any I, negative when all D, else masked
labels.no_truth: no source truth exists; source truth and ML predictions never repair labels
labels.overlap: a byte that is both executed and observed as a read / DMA source stays code (E); the overlap is counted and disclosed, never silently treated as exclusive
labels.tiers: E executed I/c strong code; R static reach weak code; H hardware header strong data; M DMA-source strong data; W ordinary ROM read weak nonexclusive data; U unknown/masked

coverage: E instruction starts and continuation bytes
cumulative executed-PC growth at 25/50/75/100 % of the emulated time
CPU seconds per extra strong code cell

novelty.primary: N_struct_not_in_control = |(forms U cfg) of the TAS strong labels  minus  the registry  minus  the seed-1 control strong labels| (cfg tuples need a LABELLED target form, so partial coverage cannot create signatures; n-grams and boundary patterns are descriptive; N_struct against the registry alone is reported beside it)
references: SEG-072 qualified development registry (target excluded by construction)
earlier games of this batch (TAS strong labels)
signatures: cfg = (flow kind, target distance class or indirect, source form, target form)
boundary = (form before data, log2 data-run bucket, form after data), taken from the weak variant because strong labels never abut code with data (descriptive only)

arms.C: base + seed-1 control strong labels of the qualified games
arms.T_matched: sensitivity: TAS strong labels randomly down-sampled (seed 81) to the control's positive and negative cell counts

model_a.budget: one fit per arm per fold; no search, no models B/C, no SEG-077 retraining
model_a.folds: leave-one-lineage-out over every qualified SEG-072 lineage (D01 included); train = other lineages (truth) + the arm's new-game labels
model_a.isolation: new-game lineage ids and image SHA-256 must be absent from the registry; 12-byte-shingle containment of labelled code runs between each new game and each held-out lineage must be <= 0.30 in both directions, else that game is withheld from that fold
model_a.metrics: per-lineage and pooled AP (primary) and AUC; positive-cell false-negative rate; negative and hard-negative false-positive rates; worst-lineage delta; error concentration; sample-volume sensitivity (T_matched)
model_a.model: SEG-072 model A / M1 HistGradientBoosting (frozen HGB_CONFIG), masked cells excluded
model_a.operating_point: threshold = the 10th percentile of B0 scores over the fold's positive cells (B0 recall 0.90); every arm scored at it

verdict.ML_GAIN_SUPPORTED: AP(T)-AP(B0) >= 0.005 and AP(T)-AP(C) >= 0.003 and worst-lineage AP(T)-AP(B0) >= -0.02 and macro FN(T) <= FN(B0)+0.01 and macro FP(T) <= FP(B0)+0.002 and AP(T_matched)-AP(B0) >= half of AP(T)-AP(B0) (otherwise volume-confounded -> ML_INCONCLUSIVE)
verdict.ML_HARM_SUPPORTED: AP(T)-AP(B0) <= -0.005 or (worst-lineage AP(T)-AP(B0) < -0.02 and pooled AP(T) < AP(B0)) or macro FN(T) > FN(B0)+0.02 or macro FP(T) > FP(B0)+0.005

precedence: INPUT_REQUIRED (input missing OR identity mismatch: the game is rejected, not replayed), BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, REPLAY_INVALID, TRACING_UNAVAILABLE, LABEL_POLICY_CONFLICT, then QUALIFIED_*
privacy: ROMs, movies, traces, labels, signatures, screenshots, per-address lists and weights stay in the ignored private directory; committed output is aggregate counts, identities (hashes), digests, hours, and the decision

replay.checkpoints: five checkpoints at floor(k*N/6) for k=1..5 plus the final completion state at frame N; each records work-RAM, VRAM, CRAM and VSRAM digests and the cumulative executed-PC / read / edge counts

gate_a.determinism: two traced TAS runs have identical PC-set, read-set, edge-set, CDL digests and checkpoint digests
gate_a.no_perturbation: playback and traced checkpoint digests (RAM, VRAM, CRAM, VSRAM) are identical at every checkpoint; a digest that is "na" (unreadable domain) or a missing domain invalidates the gate
gate_a.played_to_end: playback and traced runs both emulate exactly N frames and the playback run reports the movie FINISHED
gate_a.progression: >= 5 of the 6 checkpoint states have pairwise distinct (RAM, VRAM) digests AND at least 0.5 %% of the run's distinct ROM PCs are first executed in each of >= 3 of the 5 equal movie-time fifths

gate_tracing.controls: frames == N, map mismatch 0, odd PCs 0, reset and vblank PCs executed, self-fetch and CDL bounds

replay.playback: an untraced playback of the movie gives the reference end state (movie FINISHED at frame N) and the unperturbed checkpoint digests
replay.window: the complete movie from power-on (frames = movie input rows)

review: independent plan review before the first trace; reproduction and delta review before acceptance (synthetic CDL fixture, per-game fingerprints, marginal counts, identities, tier provenance, novelty, overlap and lineage isolation, ceilings, privacy, CI)

usefulness.extra_strong_code_cells: TAS strong code-positive cells minus the seed-1 control's (set difference, no truth filter)
usefulness.rule: extra >= 100  OR  (extra >= 25 AND extra >= 0.20 * control cells)
usefulness.sensitivity: the seed-2 control is reported (extra cells, usefulness) but never changes the primary class
usefulness.weak_labels: never counted towards the strong-code rule; data-only and mixed-cell yields are reported separately
